source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1048 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1048 was established by Ordinance No. 31804, passed by the Dallas City Council on March 24, 2021. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1048 is established on property generally bounded by Beckley Avenue, Iowa Avenue, and the Old Interurban Railway right-of-way. The size of PD 1048 is approximately 1.761 acres. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Purpose
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.103. PURPOSE.

This district is designed to encourage walkable, mixed-use, sustainable, urban development; to reduce the need for parking and promote a walkable lifestyle; to protect the surrounding neighborhood, and to support economic development in the neighborhood. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) In this article:

(1) ART OR CRAFT PRODUCTION FACILITY means a facility for the production of handcrafted art or craft products through processes such as kiln firing, glass blowing, welding, or woodworking, and for the sale of the produced products to the general public with a maximum floor area of 2,000 square feet. This use may not be combined with a residential use within the same building.

(2) LIVE/WORK UNIT means an interior space that combines a single occupancy residential use and an office or retail and personal service use and is considered a nonresidential use.

(3) STOOP means a porch, platform, entrance stairway, or small veranda on a residence.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(d) This district is considered to be a non-residential zoning district. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.105. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit 1048A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit 1048B: mixed use development (MUD) parking chart. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 1048A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MU-1 Mixed Use District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MU-1 Mixed Use District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MU-1 Mixed Use District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MU-1 Mixed Use District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following additional main uses are permitted by right.

-- Art or craft production facility. -- Live/work unit. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory use is not permitted:

-- General waste incinerator. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MU-1 Mixed Use District apply.

(b) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 15 feet.

(c) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yard is:

(1) 20 feet where adjacent to or directly across an alley from an R, R(A), D, D(A), TH, TH(A), CH, MF, or MF(A) district; and

(2) no minimum rear yard adjacent to the Old Interurban Railway right-of-way.

(3) no minimum side or rear yard in all other cases.

(d) Encroachments. The following are permitted to be located within the required front, side, and rear yards:

(1) Seat walls, retaining walls, stoops, porches, steps, unenclosed balconies, ramps, handrails, safety railings, and benches all not exceeding four feet in height and extending a maximum of five feet into the required minimum yards.

(2) Landscape and tree planters.

(3) Sculptures.

(4) Awnings.

(5) Bicycle racks.

(e) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 18.

(f) Height.

(1) Except as otherwise provide, maximum structure height is 60 feet.

(2) Maximum structure height within 80 feet of the northern property line is 26 feet.

(g) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not included in lot coverage calculations.

(h) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(i) Stories. No maximum number of stories. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Art or craft production facility. One space per 500 square feet of floor area is required.

(c) Live/work unit. One space per bedroom is required.

(d) Mixed use development parking reduction.

(1) In general.

(A) The off-street parking requirement for a mixed use development may be reduced in accordance with the mixed use development (MUD) parking chart (Exhibit 1048B).

(B) For purposes of this section, mixed use development means a tract with more than one main use.

(C) The off-street parking reduction may be used in combination with other parking reductions, except that the required parking for a mixed use development may not be reduced by more than 30 percent.

(2) Calculation of adjusted standard off-street parking requirement. The adjusted off-street parking requirement for a mixed use development is calculated as follows:

(A) First, the standard parking requirements for each of the uses in the mixed use development must be ascertained.

(B) Next, the parking demand for each use is determined for each of the times of day shown in the mixed use development (MUD) parking chart by multiplying the standard off-street parking requirement for each use by the percentage in the chart assigned to the category of use. If a use in the development does not fall within one of the categories shown in the

mixed use development (MUD) parking chart, the percentage assigned to that use is 100 percent for all times of day.

(C) Finally, the “time of day” columns are totalled to produce sums that represent the aggregate parking demand for the development at each time of day. The largest of these sums is the adjusted off-street parking requirement for the development.

(3) Minimum parking requirement. If one or more of the main uses in a mixed use development is a retail or personal service use, the minimum parking requirement for the mixed use development cannot be reduced to a number of spaces that is less than the sum of the standard parking spaces required for each of the retail and personal service uses in the mixed use development. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Urban Design Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.114. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) Public realm design.

(1) Sidewalks.

(A) Beckley Avenue. A minimum eight foot wide unobstructed sidewalk must be provided. An additional minimum landscape buffer of five feet must be provided between the back of curb and the sidewalk.

(B) Iowa Avenue. A minimum six foot wide unobstructed sidewalk must be provided. An additional minimum landscape buffer of three feet must be provided between the back of curb and sidewalk.

(C) Continuity. Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk, subject to approval by the director of public works.

(2) Pedestrian amenities.

(A) A minimum of two of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along street-facing facades, with the exception of visibility triangles and vehicular drives, in order to promote pedestrian activity and safety:

(i) benches;

(ii) bicycle racks;

(iii) trash receptacles; or

(iv) pet waste station.

(B) Pedestrian amenities may be located within the landscape buffer zone but may not obstruct the required sidewalk clear zone.

(3) Street trees. Street trees must be provided within the landscape buffer zone and must be spaced 30 feet on center wherever utilities and other subsurface conditions do not prohibit.

(4) Mechanical equipment.

(A) Aboveground utility boxes, generators, and other large mechanical equipment should, to the extent possible, be located out of view from the public right-of-way. When conditions do not permit, equipment must be screened from view by a minimum six foot high solid wood or masonry fence, wall, or building element with landscaping such as shrubs, bushes, and tress.

(B) No utilities may be placed within the required sidewalk planting zone or clear zone.

(5) Lighting.

(A) Unless otherwise provided, lighting must be spaced 75 to 100 feet apart. Spacing may be adjusted to achieve optimal photometric performance of a minimum of 0.5- foot candles between fixtures, with the exception of visibility triangles and vehicular drives.

(B) Lighting must be directed downward and away from adjacent properties.

(C) The property owner is responsible for the cost of installation, operation, and maintenance of the lighting.

(6) Open space requirements.

(A) A minimum of 10 percent of the building site must be reserved as open space for activity such as active or passive recreation, playground activity, groundwater recharge, or landscaping.

(i) Open space must be contiguous and visible from the street with direct access from the sidewalk.

(ii) Open space must be publicly accessible or unrestricted open space.

(B) A minimum of three of the following amenities must be provided:

(i) benches;

(ii) bicycle racks;

(iii) trash receptacles;

(iv) pet waste stations; or

(v) pedestrian lighting.

(C) Except as provided, in this subparagraph, open space must be open to the sky and structures are prohibited in open space except for the following:

(i) architectural elements;

(ii) playground equipment;

(iii) colonnades, pergolas, and gazebos; or

(iv) window projections.

(D) Open space must contain primarily grass, vegetation, or open water; be primarily used as a ground-water recharge area; or contain pedestrian amenities such as fountains, benches, paths, or shade structures.

(E) Open space may also be provided at or below grade or aboveground by an outside playground area, pool area, walking trail, or similar type of outside common area.

(F) Private balconies, sidewalks, parking spaces, parking lots, drive aisles, and areas primarily intended for vehicular use are not considered open space and do not count towards the open space requirement.

(G) Operation or parking of vehicles within on-site open space is prohibited. Emergency and grounds maintenance vehicles are exempt.

(7) Architectural elements. A minimum of 40 percent transparency is required for all street-facing facades located within the first 20 feet of the building at ground-level.

(8) Service and loading.

(A) Service entries and back of house functions must be located away from primary facades and must be visually screened with landscaping such as shrubs, bushes, and trees.

(B) Loading areas and loading docks must be located away from primary street facades and pedestrian routes and provide a closable gate or door that can block the loading area from the sidewalk during times when it is not in use.

(9) Surface parking. Surface parking is prohibited between the street-facing facade and the property line. For buildings with more than two street frontages, only two street frontages are subject to this requirement.

(10) Pedestrian paths. A handicap accessible continuous pedestrian path must be maintained between residential uses and Beckley Avenue.

(11) Screening. A minimum six-foot-high wood fence must be maintained along the northern Property line. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31804)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1048.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31804)
